purpose: Adjudicate Addy Osmani's current 24-Skill software-engineering catalog without restoring the deprecated adapted payloads, bulk-installing a lifecycle, duplicating current official routes, or treating upstream CI and declared evals as current cross-host value evidence.

source.acquisition: single exact-commit fetch into a bare non-active Git object root

catalogSurface.reason: Eleven Skill bodies reference repository-root reference or orchestration files outside their individual Skill directories. Exact selective admission must fetch and project the referenced bytes as a bounded composition or use a host-native whole-plugin route; a name-only directory copy is incomplete.

upstreamQualityEvidence.behavioralEvalMode: on-demand headless Claude executor and grader

checks.name: Validate command parity and description sync

upstreamQualityEvidence.claimBoundary: The exact commit has strong maintained structural, packaging, and lexical-routing evidence plus per-Skill behavioral fixtures. The repository does not commit the on-demand behavioral results, and none of this proves current Codex, Claude, Kimi, or other-host loading, causation, net value, or conflict-free composition.

pluginAndHookBoundary.reason: A CC Switch Skill admission is not permission to import the repository's Claude hook control plane. Codex explicitly declares an empty hook configuration, while Claude's session-start injection would make the rigid meta-router ambient and therefore requires a separate host-specific conflict and lifecycle review.

currentOverlap.rule: Do not duplicate a current healthy official or already-managed route merely because the Addy catalog is coherent. Preserve distinct instruction-only candidates and composition inputs for bounded same-task comparison.

legacyDerivativeComparison.reason: The old records corroborate recurring demand for these five domains, but every retained body differs from current upstream. They remain historical selection evidence only; current admission uses exact upstream bytes and current overlap/dependency review.

decision.reason: The existing exact-upstream, minimal-sufficiency, default-disabled, behavior-comparison process already expresses the needed gates. Addy supplies several strong reusable units and useful routing/evaluation architecture, but not evidence for a 24-Skill blanket lifecycle or ambient meta-router.

items.name: api-and-interface-design
items.reason: Standalone and useful, but its universal REST and interface defaults overlap current domain/codebase design routes and need a real design task comparison before shared admission.

items.name: browser-testing-with-devtools
items.reason: Current browser, Chrome, and Playwright routes are visible; this body additionally assumes a separately configured Chrome DevTools MCP, which is a task-time lifecycle and resource boundary.

items.name: ci-cd-and-automation
items.reason: A dependency-free generic pipeline and rollout workflow with historical demand evidence. Any workflow write, secret boundary, deployment, or account action remains separately task-authorized.

items.name: code-review-and-quality
items.reason: Current Superpowers review routes, managed code-review, and official security routes already cover the domain; a directory-only copy would also omit two upstream checklists.

items.name: code-simplification
items.reason: The standalone behavior-preserving simplification workflow may add value, but overlaps disciplined-coding, code review, and refactor planning and cites an upstream official Claude simplifier as prior art.

items.name: context-engineering
items.reason: Directly relevant to the Harness context lifecycle lane, but it mixes rules-file, conversation, and planning advice. Compare it against Kimi prototypes and host-native compression/handoff before deciding whether a shared Skill is needed.

items.name: debugging-and-error-recovery
items.reason: Superpowers systematic-debugging and the managed diagnosing-bugs route already cover reproduce-localize-fix-verify.

items.name: deprecation-and-migration
items.reason: A dependency-free, distinct migration and retirement workflow with historical demand evidence. Destructive migration or removal remains outside Skill authority.

items.name: documentation-and-adrs
items.reason: A dependency-free engineering-decision workflow distinct from document file manipulation; it first defers to existing repository ADR conventions.

items.name: doubt-driven-development
items.reason: Its bounded fresh-context adversarial review is relevant, but each interactive cycle mandates a cross-model offer and may spawn reviewers or external CLIs. Treat it as topology/resource-governance input until cost, route, nesting, observer, and cleanup gates are composed.

items.name: frontend-ui-engineering
items.reason: Current official product-design and sites routes cover UI and accessibility work; the selective payload also depends on a root checklist.

items.name: git-workflow-and-versioning
items.reason: Superpowers worktree/branch workflows plus repository Git discipline already govern this consequential surface; a generic Skill cannot override repository truth or commit/push authority.

items.name: idea-refine
items.reason: Superpowers brainstorming is already current; Addy's only executable Skill also creates docs/ideas when its optional helper runs, so it is not the minimal duplicate.

items.name: incremental-implementation
items.reason: Superpowers plan execution, TDD, and subagent workflows already cover incremental implementation; the selective payload also omits the repository Definition of Done.

items.name: interview-me
items.reason: The current exact Matt grilling route already provides bounded requirements interrogation. A same-task comparison may revisit this only if a concrete failure appears.

items.name: observability-and-instrumentation
items.reason: Distinct generic operations value and historical demand evidence, but exact selective admission must atomically include its root checklist without rewriting either file.

items.name: performance-optimization
items.reason: Generic measurement-first performance value and historical demand evidence, but exact selective admission must atomically include its root checklist and later compare against current vendor-specific performance routes.

items.name: planning-and-task-breakdown
items.reason: Superpowers already supplies plan writing/execution. This body requires Plan mode and fixed tasks/plan.md plus tasks/todo.md outputs, which is not a universal host or user workflow and omits its root Definition of Done under selective copy.

items.name: security-and-hardening
items.reason: The current official Codex Security plugin provides specialized security routing and validation; this selective payload also omits its root security checklist.

items.name: shipping-and-launch
items.reason: Useful launch guidance, but it carries fixed rollout thresholds, production side-effect examples, and four root dependencies. Keep for a bound launch comparison rather than shared admission now.

items.name: source-driven-development
items.reason: A dependency-free, vendor-neutral current-documentation workflow not replaced by the OpenAI-specific docs route. Network use and source selection remain task-time data and authority boundaries.

items.name: spec-driven-development
items.reason: Its gated living-spec workflow and fixed task files are useful comparison material, but should not become an ambient hard constraint over iterative or exploratory work; compare with Matt's cache-like spec posture and Superpowers only on bound tasks.

items.name: test-driven-development
items.reason: Superpowers TDD and a managed TDD route are already visible; Addy's selective file also omits the referenced testing patterns.

items.name: using-agent-skills
items.reason: Its ambient rules say workflows are mandatory, route almost all work through Skills, and default non-trivial work to specs. That conflicts with native-first minimal sufficiency and event-driven dynamic discovery; use as a router test input, not an installed meta-authority.

nextGate: Keep four standalone and two dependency-complete composition candidates inactive behind the CC Switch atomic default-disabled gap, then continue the bounded cohort with JimLiu/baoyu-skills.
